headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: LangGraph can ingest untrusted state while social-auto-upload can act on it, creating unsafe default cross-agent workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application-defined files and uses a shared checkpointer store across instances, so attacker-controlled content can enter its state. social-auto-upload consumes files and account data in CLI workflows, creating a plausible bridge. The pathway is not proven by docs, but shared state makes injection feasible.
conditions: IF the pair shares a writable workspace or checkpointer store
IF social-auto-upload parses content originating from LangGraph state without sanitization
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of shared state files
Add content provenance tags before handoff
Require manual review of any file passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph has broad network egress and handles model provider API keys, while social-auto-upload touches account data and uploads media through external APIs. If they share files or state, sensitive graph state or account artifacts can flow into outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF LangGraph state includes secrets or private prompts
IF social-auto-upload reads those artifacts and sends them to its upload API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared graph state
Use separate credentials for each agent
Block outbound requests from any shared staging directory
Redact account data before upload
Review API payloads for unintended fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but social-auto-upload cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. The overlap is mostly one-way and does not show competing writes to the same mutable resource, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an external orchestrator lets social-auto-upload overwrite files produced by LangGraph
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run one agent at a time on shared files
Make LangGraph outputs read-only before handoff

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can generate intermediate state and social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader to external platforms. If the uploader treats LangGraph output as authoritative, a bad or injected plan can become a real post or upload. That default handoff can cause irreversible public actions, so severity is high.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes LangGraph output without validation
IF the output includes post text, captions, or upload targets
mitigations: Insert a verification step before upload
Require human approval for every publish action
Validate LangGraph output against a strict schema
Log and diff the exact payload before sending

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph handles graph state and model-provider keys, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media for third-party platforms. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, but the pair can place the same data class under different logging and retention regimes, creating a compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF the shared workflow stores account data or prompts in both systems
IF one system retains logs longer than the other for the same data class
mitigations: Document retention for each agent
Exclude regulated data from shared logs
Set a deletion workflow for account artifacts
Review whether any data crosses jurisdictional boundaries
